title: Analysis of Supply Chain Risk and Enhancing Sustainability in the Medical Sector in Bangladesh Due to Russia‐Ukraine War
content: Purpose: The study examines how the Russia-Ukraine war affects the medical supply chain in Bangladesh. It aims to identify risks and propose strategies for a sustainable supply chain amid the conflict. Design / Methodology / Approach: The research used AHP and SWARA methods to analyze 30 risk factors, selecting six based on expert opinions. AHP determined their significance, while SWARA assessed weights and ranked their impact on supply chain sustainability. Findings: Increasing fuel costs are the top risk, followed by economic risks. Transportation and logistics management risks ranked third, with demand, relationship, and sustainability risks following. These vulnerabilities emphasize targeted risk management strategies in Bangladesh's medical supply chain due to the war. Research limitations/implications: The study's focus on Bangladesh's healthcare sector limits insight into the broad impact of the Russia-Ukraine conflict on supply chains. Relying on expert opinions may introduce bias. Practical Implications: The research offers valuable guidance for medical industry leaders to address supply chain risks effectively amid geopolitical conflicts. Other sectors can also benefit from these strategies. Originality/Value: The study uses AHP and SWARA to evaluate supply chain risks during geopolitical conflicts, focusing on challenges in Bangladesh's medical sector and offering insights to improve resilience, management, and contributing to agricultural sector growth and food security in Bangladesh.
